historical_references.reference: Wissam was a title given to the military governors of Egypt during the Fatimid Caliphate, which ruled Egypt from 969 to 1171 AD. The title signified a person who guaranteed the safety and security of the land and its people.

Wissam was also a title given to the Arabian poet and historian Al-Wassam Ibn Laban Al-Khafaji (896-940 AD) during the Abbasid Caliphate. He is known for his poetic works and historical accounts of the early Islamic period in Iraq and Syria.
